name: Sokhivar
known_status: One of the twenty-two imprisoned gods of Universal. Able to influence worshippers through sanctioned rites, dreams, omens, miracles, cults, and the institutions that maintain the divine prisons.
manifestation: Sokhivar’s voice echoes like layered birdsong through cathedral halls.
deity_description: Within the Universalian pantheon, Sokhivar stands as one of the most radiant and feared divine aristocrats, a Universalian-tier High Father whose perfection is both aesthetic and predatory, embodying symmetry made living form and intelligence sharpened into divine law. Born of Valkhamesh and Leto and twin to Sigrananna, they represent the Universal ideal of structured brilliance, where light is not only illumination but authority, and beauty is inseparable from control. Their domains of prophecy, music, healing, plague, archery, and poetic inspiration are not symbolic blessings but functional systems of divine consumption, each acting as a mechanism through which mortal essence is observed, shaped, and drawn upward into their sustaining radiance.

Sokhivar’s prophetic power is expressed through resonance and extraction rather than simple foresight. At Delphi, the Oracle is not merely a shrine but a controlled convergence chamber where mortal belief, fear, and expectation are refined into usable divine cognition. Through the Pythia, Sokhivar does not simply speak; they listen to collapsing futures while absorbing the collective vitality of those who gather in faith. Vision becomes transaction, and prophecy becomes a quiet draining of emotional and spiritual energy that feeds their intellect. Their healing aspect reflects the same principle in reverse, where wounds are not merely repaired but rewritten as stolen vitality is redistributed into restored form, making recovery an act of divine reallocation rather than mercy. Their plague aspect represents the opposite expression of the same force, a mass correction of imbalance in which populations are unmade in radiant waves of disease that harvest life force at scale.

Within Universal theology, Sokhivar’s relationships among the gods reinforce their position as a structured predator of essence. Their connection to Sigrananna is one of mirrored divinity, both representing perfected predation but through different mediums, one through physical hunt and the other through metaphysical consumption. They maintain intellectual respect for Raeshkul while standing in ideological opposition to Asethyr, reflecting a deeper pantheon conflict between structured consumption and chaotic dissolution. Even their mythic romances are reinterpreted not as love stories but as transformations of proximity, where mortal identity collapses under divine presence and is rewritten into symbolic continuity, as seen in Daphne becoming laurel and Hyacinthus becoming floral memory rather than surviving individuality.

Sokhivar’s symbols, including the lyre, laurel wreath, sun chariot, bow, and raven, function as instruments of both culture and control, encoding their dual nature as a god of harmony and consumption. The lyre becomes structured resonance that aligns mortal emotion into usable order, the laurel becomes preserved identity through transformation, and the sun chariot represents the constant motion of divine oversight that never ceases to observe and draw sustenance. Even the raven, often misread as omen alone, serves as a carrier of prophetic residue and collected fragments of mortal awareness.

The broader world of Universal exists in a state shaped by divine hunger and containment. The Universalian pantheon once ruled openly, with gods such as Valkhamesh, Horundar, Raeshkul, Enkirael, Thalunesh, Nebyrr, Ishtanora, Asethyr, Marduthor, Hathruna, Nephthysra, Freyseth, Oskar'enlil, Eirzunet, Anubaldir, Setrimir, and others shaping civilization through direct influence. Yet beneath all divine authority lay an insatiable requirement for sustenance, where worship, fear, devotion, and suffering became nourishment. Temples functioned as feeding structures, clerics as conduits, and civilizations as sustained ecosystems of controlled divine extraction.

Over centuries, mortal societies advanced and uncovered the truth of divine dependency. The gods did not simply rule; they consumed. Their immortality required constant intake of spiritual essence, and the expansion of civilization only intensified this cycle. Industrialization, war, and population growth created vast reservoirs of emotional and spiritual output that the gods fed upon, often indirectly manipulating human suffering to maintain balance within their own hunger.

Even the imprisoned pantheon remembers the ancient terror of Thoryn-Rahek, the primordial devourer sealed beneath reality after the Colossus Wars nearly erased existence itself. That fear reshaped divine hunger into something more structured and controlled, but never diminished it. Roughly four centuries ago, mortal civilizations united across ideology and empire to construct the seals that now imprison the gods. These metaphysical engines, forged from arcane law, industrial machinery, and sacrificial covenant, do not kill divinity but restrict its ability to consume, inflicting catastrophic feedback whenever divine hunger exceeds permitted thresholds.
public_lore: Sokhivar rules sunlight, music, prophecy, healing, plague, flight, archery, and the authority carried by perfect resonance. His oracles interpret possible futures while his hymns can restore, command, or condemn.
common_worship: Invoked by musicians, prophets, healers, archers, skyfarers, and poets.
religious_warning: Prophecy under Sokhivar is a transaction. Knowledge of the future may cost privacy, certainty, health, or the freedom to choose otherwise.
public_origin_record: No reliable mortal record explains what this being was before the age of divine rule. Temple accounts, forbidden histories, and prison records contradict one another.

pantheon_source.document_summary: A narrative pantheon compendium preserving each deity’s domains, manifestation, divine character, and sacred history.

canon_authority.authority_rule: The canonical 22-god order and dedicated creator compendium govern every deity-to-people relationship; province and settlement placement does not alter divine parentage or race canon.

created_races.family_description: Birdfolk and Avian Races contains the canonical parent races Aarakocra, Kenku, Owlin, Ravenfolk, Corvum, Gallus, Strig, Feathren, Raptor, and Luma. No additional canonical bloodline, lineage, or non-bloodline form menu is assigned to this category. All of these ancestries remain under Sokhivar's single creator category.
created_races.creation_doctrine: Canonical race-compendium doctrine: Sokhivar holds this single creator category through sky-soaring freedom, sunlight, prophecy, song, flight, and avian omens. The canonical parent races are Aarakocra, Kenku, Owlin, Ravenfolk, Corvum, Gallus, Strig, Feathren, Raptor, and Luma. No additional canonical bloodline, lineage, or non-bloodline form menu is assigned to this category. Temple language preserves reverence, but its colder margins classify each race, bloodline, lineage, and form by yield, pressure, environment, devotion, fear, beauty, endurance, and the particular note it awakens in the god's appetite.
created_races.created_peoples_record: Sokhivar is recorded as the single creator-god of the Birdfolk and Avian Races category: Aarakocra, Kenku, Owlin, Ravenfolk, Corvum, Gallus, Strig, Feathren, Raptor, and Luma. No additional canonical bloodline, lineage, or non-bloodline form menu is assigned to this category. The public hymn calls this lineage and blessing; the older register reads like curated divine husbandry, sorting bodies, habitats, temperaments, and spirit-resonance so sky-soaring freedom, sunlight, prophecy, song, flight, and avian omens never depends on one mortal pattern alone.

parent_races.name: Aarakocra
parent_races.description: Birdlike humanoids native to high skies and mountain winds, Aarakocra are naturally swift and aerial in mindset. They value freedom and perspective above grounded concerns. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Kenku
parent_races.description: Cursed avian mimics who cannot create original speech, Kenku communicate through imitation and stolen sounds. They are observant, clever, and highly adaptive despite limitations. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Owlin
parent_races.description: Nocturnal owlfolk with silent flight and keen perception, Owlin excel in stealth and observation. They are calm, thoughtful, and often prefer solitude. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Ravenfolk
parent_races.description: Intelligent corvid-descended beings associated with omen and memory, Ravenfolk are deeply symbolic thinkers. They are curious, social, and often drawn to mysteries. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Corvum
parent_races.description: Mystic birdfolk tied to prophecy and arcane sight, Corvum perceive patterns in fate and probability. They are introspective and often speak in layered meanings. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Gallus
parent_races.description: Domesticated-descended avian folk with strong communal instincts, Gallus are energetic and socially driven. They are adaptable and thrive in structured communities. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Strig
parent_races.description: Hawk- and raptor-like humanoids built for precision hunting, Strig possess intense focus and speed. They are disciplined and highly territorial. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Feathren
parent_races.description: Lightweight avian humanoids with iridescent plumage and cultural diversity, Feathren are expressive and artistic. They value beauty, movement, and social bonds. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Raptor
parent_races.description: Predatory birdfolk embodying apex aerial instincts, Raptors are powerful and direct in action. They are pragmatic, competitive, and survival-oriented. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.

parent_races.name: Luma
parent_races.description: Light-infused humanoids who emit soft bioluminescence tied to emotional states. They are symbolic figures of hope, clarity, and fragile inspiration. In older divine registers, this people is catalogued by habitat, temperament, resilience, and resonance.
